record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-regular graph that is Class 2, meaning it is not edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 (Ma, Mattiolo, Steffen, Wolf [1]) Is there any 5-edge-connected 5-regular Class 2 graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is said to be $k$-regular if every vertex has degree exactly $k$, and $k$-edge-connected if removing any set of fewer than $k$ edges leaves the graph connected. The chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color the edges of $G$ so that no two edges sharing a vertex receive the same color. By Vizing's theorem, $\chi'(G) \in \{\Delta(G), \Delta(G)+1\}$, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree. A graph $G$ is called Class 1 if $\chi'(G) = \Delta(G)$ and Class 2 if $\chi'(G) = \Delta(G)+1$.

Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-regular graph that is Class 2 (i.e., whose chromatic index equals $6$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in workshop problem collections and is closely connected with conjectures (Berge–Fulkerson, Fan–Raspaud) for 5-edge-connected 5-regular graphs studied by Ma, Mattiolo, Steffen and Wolf. No resolution (either an example or a proof of non-existence) appears in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Pairwise Disjoint Perfect Matchings in r-Edge-Connected r-Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Relates statements on pairwise disjoint perfect matchings of 5-edge-connected 5-regular graphs to conjectures for cubic graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/structure problems for 5-edge-connected 5-regular graphs are an active topic with no known Class 2 example.

status_evidence.title: Edge colorings and circular flows on regular graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies chromatic index of regular graphs and edge connectivity conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of Class 2 examples in higher edge-connectivity regimes remains an open question.
